newsitem.title: POLAND: New Polish farm minister wants lower EU tariffs.
newsitem.headline: New Polish farm minister wants lower EU tariffs.

text.p: Poland's new agriculture minister wants the European Union (EU) to lower its customs tariffs on Polish farm products such as meat, private Radio Zet reported on Sunday.

The radio quoted Jaroslaw Kalinowski as telling a news conference of his Polish Peasant Party (PSL) that the EU should decrease tarrifs in response to Poland's plan, announced on Friday, to cut valued-added tax (VAT) on citrus imports.

"The lowering of VAT (on citrus fruit) from 22 to seven percent from January 1998 is to some extent reasonable, but it should be tied to decisions by the other side to let our goods flow into that market," Kalinowski said.

Friday's proposal by the government's European Integration Committee must be approved at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, where Kalinowski said he would call on the government to raise Poland's tariffs on imported EU starch to 40 from 15 percent.
Tariff issues are expected to be discussed at a European Union-Poland Association Council meeting in Luxembourg later this week.
Kalinowski was appointed agriculture minister last Friday, saying his priorities would be tough accession talks with the EU and new measures to protect Poland's farm market.
He replaced the more liberal-minded Roman Jagielinski. Both men are members of the co-ruling PSL.
